questions.stem: A billing job runs `try (var lock = locks.acquire("invoice-7731"); var conn = db.connect()) { charge(conn); } catch (DeclinedException e) { notifyCustomer(e); }`. The call to charge() throws DeclinedException. While notifyCustomer() runs, what state are the lock and the connection in?

options.text: Both are still held, since the catch belongs to the same statement whose header acquired them
options.says: the catch belongs to the statement, and the statement closes its resources before the catch runs

options.text: Both are released, since the statement closes what its header declared before its catch runs
options.says: the resources are closed, in reverse order, before the statement's catch and finally run

options.text: Only the connection is closed, since the lock is released after the catch, last in reverse order
options.says: reverse order applies among the resources; all of them are closed before the catch runs

options.text: Only the lock is released, since it was declared first and resources close in the order they appear
options.says: resources close in reverse order of declaration, and all of them before the catch

origin.section: Resources Close in Reverse Order, Before the Statement's catch and finally Run

questions.stem: An export runs a query inside `try (Connection conn = pool.getConnection()) { ... }`. The query throws SQLTimeoutException("query timed out"), and then conn.close() throws SQLException("connection reset"). The caller catches the exception and logs `"export failed: " + e.getMessage()`. What does the log line say?

options.text: export failed: query timed out, since the body's exception is thrown and the close failure rides along inside it
options.says: the body's exception is thrown, and the close failure is only in its getSuppressed(), which getMessage() does not include

options.text: export failed: query timed out; connection reset, since the close failure is added to the message of the exception thrown
options.says: addSuppressed attaches the close failure as an object; the message of the thrown exception is unchanged

options.text: export failed: connection reset, since the close runs after the query and its exception takes the place of the earlier one
options.says: that is what a close in finally does; try-with-resources keeps the body's exception and suppresses the close failure

options.text: export failed: connection reset, since a close failure is reported first and the failure it hides is attached to it
options.says: it is the other way round: the body's exception is thrown and the close failure is attached to it

origin.section: A close() Failure Is Attached as Suppressed, Not Thrown in Place of the Body's Exception

questions.stem: A cache loader runs `try (ObjectInputStream in = new ObjectInputStream(new FileInputStream(file))) { return in.readObject(); }`. One cache file is empty, so ObjectInputStream's constructor throws EOFException. What becomes of the FileInputStream opened for it?

options.text: The statement closes it, since a stream passed to a resource's constructor in the header is closed with that resource
options.says: only the declared variable is a resource; a stream created as a constructor argument is not, and here the resource never existed

options.text: The statement closes it, since a resource whose constructor throws is closed along with those declared before it
options.says: a resource whose constructor threw never existed, so there is nothing to close, and the file stream is not a resource

options.text: It stays open until a garbage collection reclaims it, since the resource the header declares was never created
options.says: the declared resource is the ObjectInputStream, which was never created, so nothing closes the file until the JDK's cleaner does after a GC

options.text: It stays open until the loader's thread ends, since the streams a thread opens are released when that thread finishes
options.says: nothing ties a stream to its thread; the descriptors came back after a full GC, when the JDK's cleaner closed the unreachable streams

origin.section: Only a Resource That Finished Constructing Is Closed, So Declare Each Stream Separately

questions.stem: A report method creates a BufferedWriter and passes it to `static void writeFooter(Writer out) throws IOException { try (out) { out.write("-- end --"); } }`. After writeFooter returns, the report method writes one more section to the same writer. What happens at that write?

options.text: It succeeds, since the statement closes only what its own header creates, and the writer came from outside
options.says: since Java 9 a statement also closes an existing variable named in its header

options.text: It succeeds, since the statement closes only what its own method opens, and the writer came from outside
options.says: the statement closes whatever it names, whoever opened it

options.text: It fails with IOException, since the statement closes what it names when its block ends, the writer included
options.says: the statement closes the variable it names, so the caller's writer is closed and the next write fails with Stream closed

options.text: It fails with IOException, since the statement closes what it names when its header runs, the writer included
options.says: the statement closes its resources when the block exits; closed at the header, the footer write itself would have failed

origin.section: A Variable Named in the Header Is Closed Too, Whoever Opened It
